Refugees in Cape Town: A Right Royal Mess

By: Michael Duffett | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How can this human drama end?

Unique Selling Point:
In october, several hundred refugees descended onto the UNCHR offices in Pretoria and Cape Town, demanding safety from xenbophobic attacks and to be flown to other parts of the world. These sits ins were halted by court action. In Pretoria 100's were arrested, in Cape Town there was pandemomium as poice physically removed the refugees. The Cape Town reguees then were invited to take refuge in the Methadist church. And they have been here for months - 400 or so women men and children in stressful contions, another 300 outside - a virtual shanty town, lining the famous Green Market SQ. Businesses in the area including the traders complain that their inocme has been reduced, one hotel says to the tune of 5 million rand due to cancalled bookings.
The City of Cape Town tried to evcit them three weeks ago, but the judge would have none of that. She was not prepared to evict children. She castigated all the stake holders and urged them to come to a soluation at the next court hearing. How this this mess been allowed to contonue so long -

Further information:
it's been very tense these last two weeks - there has been a power struggle between two factiions who have been at ezch other throats. Police have had to have a constant preence to stop vioence. The struggle is between the leader and one of this lieutnants a a dwarf. There are accusations that the main leader JP Bealus is a warlod from Africa but where is the proof.
In the meantime this sweltering sea of humanity exsists - babaies are being born...and its a real struggle for everybody in the church.
The questions that need to be asked:
why now suddnely? who instigated this? Are the demands reasonable? How has this affeced business in the area? is there any solution eecpt for a mass poice action.
How are these people coping inside? To what extent does Home Affairs have something to answer for? There is anger at the dept because of the xenophia the regugees freel from them - the uyears it takes to propcess their appications to have refugee status.

Script:


VO
While international tourists stroll along Church streets in the Mother City just 200 meters away around the corner a humanitarian crisis is playing out.

upsound

Hundreds of refugees who claim to be victims of xenophobic violence are holed up in a church and on the surrounding pavements. One of those is Julia Mushixa who has been living in a makeshift tent next to the church for the last three months with her three children. She fled the DRC 10 years ago after her father was murdered. But it hasn't been easy for her in South Africa.

Julia
Coloured guys, Xhosa guys stabbed me and take my stuff.

VO
Julia says that her small trading business was trashed several times.

Upsound

With tension spilling over into the streets during the festive season, refugees were demanding to be flown to safe haven outside of Africa.

Upsound

Just how and why has this situation got to this stage. To answer that, we need to go back to September last year when Gauteng was rocked by xenophobic attacks which saw the destructions of scores of businesses owned by foreign nationals. Appalled by the number of zenophobic incidents over the years, Aline Bukuru , who runs an NGO called Woman and Children at Concern , had discussions with other refugee leaders

Aline
With us we asked for suggestions, what do you think with them and majority of people they said that we need to vote of the U.N. because it's only this sole organization around the world that is mandated to protect refugees.

Vo
In September last year hundreds of refugees set up camp at the offices of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, commonly known as the UNHCR in Brooklyn Pretoria.
And in early October refugee started to camp outside the UNHCR offices in Cape Town. It appears that they had been sold the idea that planes would be provided by the UNHCR to fly them overseas to safety.

Leonard Zulu
The refugees had been lied to that the UNHCR was preparing buses and planes that was not true.

VO
Leonard Zulu the South African deputy head of the UNHCR said that a mass exodus of refugees from South Africa can never take place.

Leonard Zulu
The UNHCRcan not resettle the protesting refugees in mass because that is not how we process resettlement we process resettlement on an individual basis based on a very stringent and strict criteria that is established and set by the receiving countries.

VO
Following an urgent HIGH COURT EVICTION ORDER at the end of October last year, there were distressing scenes as police started to force the refugees from the UNHCR offices in Cape Town, -who then moved into the Methodist Church which flanks Green Market Square. The invitation came from Rev. Allen Storey who wanted to provide a short term safe haven . They been there ever since and living conditions are cramp and unhygienic………. Tragedy struck this community in November when four teenagers who were living in the church drowned at sea on a day's outing.

(above refers – please make sure voice over end before the coffin is seen)

Several babies have been born as well and parents have their hand full trying to care for their children in such a confined space.

SANDRA
Sometimes we sleep sitting down and also bathing we go to wipe in the toilet because there's no bathrooms inside. So its not been easy.

VO
Businesses close to the church and Green Market Square have been affected.

TOSCA Korvel
A lot of tours have cancelled a lot of group bookings have cancelled and saying that they need to wait to see if this is being resolved before they'll book with us.

VO
Tosca Korval is the general manager of a newly established hotel next to the Church.

Anna Korvel
By end of October we will on 70 per cent occupancy which means that we were more than breaking even in that month and from when they moved in it dropped down to December 40 per. Cent I have had to move guests around because of the noise, loud speakers facing the church…that’s why the drop in occupancy.

VO
And it's the same story at the famous Green Market Square. Mor Fall is the general manager of the market and he says traders have had a tough Christmas season.

Mr Fall
Most of the tourists are not coming to Green Market Square most of the hotels their clients are running away to other hotels because they think that the area is not safe.

VO
He has noticed a massive decline in sales.

Mr Fall
More than 50 percent. Some are closing their stores.


VO
And matters were not helped by a conflict that broke a few weeks ago between Papi Sukami who was appointed into a leadership position by the refugee leader Jean Pierre Balous - ,know as JP


JP BALOU
I didn't support him because he knew something I supported him because of his disability. I wanted to give him confidence.

VO
But the 42 year old Sukami was gunning for Balaus,

PAPY SUKAMI
The community are accusing him for misleading the people. Bad leadership.

VO
Sukami was a union leader in the DRC but after he is arrested for organizing a strike he managed to escape and headed for South Africa. He made several accusations against Belous including the theft of donor money. ….. Belous vehemently denies this.

BALOUS
That donation when it comes it is the one that we are using to buy their medications to buy milk for their children. Is there money that we are using to buy all sorts of toiletries and everything that we need here.

VO
SUKAMI was relentless in demanding BALOUS’ ARREST.. As a result, a split developed -Belous’s followers remained in the church while SUKAMI’S followers lived on the street outside. A strong police presence prevented violence from erupting.

On New Year's Day Belous was invited down to police headquarters for a talk and then was arrested on several charges including assault. His followers tried to storm the police station but were dispelled by stun grenades.

upsound

Chris Nissan of the Human Rights Commission was in the church in mid December when several clergy tried to encourage the refugees to return to their communities. Balous was also in the church,

CHRIS NISSEN
And then all hell broke loose. One of the ladies got onto the stage took the mike from the pastor and then the leader, JP rushed over knocked down the pastor and then there was a turn on us on the archbishop. and myself and others.

VO
Nissan was also struck but not seriously injured. Fortunately relative peace returned to the square after Sukami was also suddenly arrested for robbery. Both were later released on bail but they are forbidden to enter the CBD unless permission is granted by the police.

This is the situation the city of cape town had hoped to prevent, It had approached the high court to evict the refugees in December for non compliance of by laws … . a Cape Town a judge refused to grant the order adding that she was not prepared to evict the children. She told the main role players to return to court later in January with an amicable solution. J.P. Smith who heads up safety and security for the City said that it had offered its services to reintegrate every single refugee back into the community. But it was loath to provide temporary accommodation.

JP SMITH
There are some 286 000 known refugees in this city and probably at least double that. If you set a precedent by offering emergency accommodation to a thousand persons imperiled by in this case an act of their own making. Then you set a precedent. Why would any of the remaining two hundred and eighty six thousand plus people not then claim the same privileges or opportunities of emergency accommodation.
VO
The city also asked the court to order the dept. of home affairs to assess all the refugees and provide documentation where necessary. At this stage the department has no idea how many are undocumented.

Minister
“ we can do this in three days,,,,,,we have been unable to do this because they all came into the church. One we can find a place for them, we can find out what the situation is

VO
Minister Aron Modseledi said that there was only one way forward.

Minister: the people must return to the community, it is the only solution, and that is what the talks are about.

VO
This will be a bitter pill for Julia to swallow. She gave up her rented accommodation and came to the square to prepare for a better life in another country.

JULIA
I need to be safe here anyway. To get future for my child can be better also for me. For now I'm not fighting for my life I'm fighting for my child's life.

VO
In the mealtime, Home affairs, the UNHCR, the city, the human rights commission and refugee leaders are meeting regularly to discuss a solution. Balus said earlier week that he and his followers would vacate the church within 2 weeks because of the deteriating living conditions.

Nissan hopes that the stand off will end soon, …and that there will be no force removals


Nissan: I hope that does not happen, I pray it does not happen. These people must understand that there is no chance that the refugees can be removed

These sits ins were halted by court action. In Pretoria 100's were arrested, in Cape Town there was pandemomium as poice physically removed the refugees. The Cape Town reguees then were invited to take refuge in the Methadist church. And they have been here for months - 400 or so women men and children in stressful contions, another 300 outside - a virtual shanty town, lining the famous Green Market SQ. Businesses in the area including the traders complain that their inocme has been reduced, one hotel says to the tune of 5 million rand due to cancalled bookings. The City of Cape Town tried to evcit them three weeks ago, but the judge would have none of that. She was not prepared to evict children. She castigated all the stake holders and urged them to come to a soluation at the next court hearing. How this this mess been allowed to contonue so long -
metadata.Further information: it's been very tense these last two weeks - there has been a power struggle between two factiions who have been at ezch other throats. Police have had to have a constant preence to stop vioence. The struggle is between the leader and one of this lieutnants a a dwarf. There are accusations that the main leader JP Bealus is a warlod from Africa but where is the proof. In the meantime this sweltering sea of humanity exsists - babaies are being born...and its a real struggle for everybody in the church. The questions that need to be asked: why now suddnely? who instigated this? Are the demands reasonable? How has this affeced business in the area? is there any solution eecpt for a mass poice action. How are these people coping inside? To what extent does Home Affairs have something to answer for? There is anger at the dept because of the xenophia the regugees freel from them - the uyears it takes to propcess their appications to have refugee status.
